pix/host._prod_loc_note: Then the daemon runtime: a third [[services]] runtime for a long-running HOST process that already speaks its own protocol on a loopback port. It exists because go-plugin is the wrong shape for one -- snow-proxy is reached over HTTP by an in-sandbox wrapper, so a net/rpc handshake would replace a working transport to gain nothing -- and because the Port/Listen/Health fields on Service were designed for exactly this and had no runtime that read them. It reuses everything that matters (staged copy-then-verify, env allowlist, restart budgets, the permanent-vs-transient split, and the rule that a running process is not health) and adds only launch + probe. The doctor row is the point: a pack daemon was the one host-exec facet with NO row, so when snow-proxy died the warehouse capability degraded in total silence.

pix/host/cli._prod_loc_note: 475 -> 502: Deps.Config() now warns about config keys this build ignores, so a typo is surfaced instead of silently doing nothing. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget, which is the only way this number is allowed to move.

pix/host/cmd/pix._prod_loc_note: 3036 -> 3071: `pix resume SESSION [DIR]` turns pi's exact exit receipt into a host command without exposing `run -- --session`. Then 3071 -> 3136, edges 22 -> 23: `pix reset` is back (reset_cmd.go). The new edge is cmd/pix -> workflow/reset, and it is the whole point of the shape: reset is L3 and workflow/launch is its L3 sibling, so the command layer is the ONLY place allowed to hold both. It injects `pix rm --all` into reset as reset.Sweep rather than letting reset grow a sandbox removal of its own; that alternative would have cost no edge here and created a second bulk force-removal seam beside the one explicitly-named one. Deliberate, reviewed raises of a shrink-only budget. Then the independent-review round: three clean-slate reviewers attacked the first cut and found real gaps, all closed here. A pack's `probe` runs on the host and was in neither the fingerprint nor the consent screen, so a pack could change what pix executes without re-gating. `ActiveServerMCP` read only the LAST activated pack, so on a composed stack doctor accused half of it of being undeclared and recommended `sbx mcp rm` on servers it had just registered — and it read a pack that fails to load as a pack that declares nothing, which turned one manifest typo into that same advice for every server on the host. MCP names and probe argv[0] were the only pack identifiers not name-gated, while landing in commands users paste into a shell. `NonSecretEnvNames` excluded a secret per-integration rather than pack-wide, so one integration could allowlist another's credential into plaintext. Probes could outrun their budget with no WaitDelay, which matters precisely because they now run through `op run`. And doctor's own report said `✓ ready` over a row that had proved an integration unusable, undercounted the unknowns behind the gaps, and printed one repair when several were needed. Each fix is a few lines; the volume is that there were many, and every one was a way of claiming more than had been verified.

pix/host/config._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 796 -> 804: ServiceEnabled now resolves `services` the way `pix-host serve` does, and the load-bearing half is that EMPTY MEANS ALL (resolveServices: "an empty result means all"). Reading empty as none made doctor call memory OPTIONAL on a config where serve starts it -- the commonest config there is -- so a memory unit that was genuinely down could not fail readiness. A deliberate, reviewed raise.

pix/host/health._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 1277 -> 1286, globals 29 -> 30: the probe half of McpAuthNotRequired (see pix/host/mcp's note) -- a server that needs no OAuth is now reported as ANSWERED rather than counted against the row as unproven, which is what made the mcp row a permanent `?`. pix/host/inference._prod_loc_note: raised together for ONE change: `pix doctor` and `pix setup` demanded an anthropic/openai/google key from hosts whose models need none. A pack's sbx-session backends carry their own credential (a Docker login session the sbx proxy injects inside the sandbox, unreplayable from the host by design), so the key store lists nothing and the required row went red prescribing `pix models add anthropic` -- a key nothing would read. `pix run`'s launch gate already skipped the key check on exactly this host (inference.ConfiguredKeylessInference); ProviderKeyProbe.Keyless + inference.KeylessBackends give the same carve-out to the two verbs that lacked it, so all three stop disagreeing about one host. Distinct from Callable, which answers "this key routes nowhere"; Keyless answers "no key was ever the credential". provision's new edge is importing inference for that one predicate rather than re-deriving a second opinion. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget.

pix/host/service._prod_loc_note: 1664 -> 1708: `serve stop` now sweeps for orphaned `pix-host serve` processes AFTER stopping the pid its pidfile recorded. A pidfile names one daemon and is not proof there is only one, so a second daemon outliving its own pidfile kept holding :11435 while stop reported success. That is why `pix serve stop` had to be run twice. The sweep only ever signals pids that positively verify as our live serve. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget. Then reset's post-stop settle: a launchd boot-out returns when the unit is unloaded, not when the process has exited, and this daemon closes a sqlite writer and reaps a supervised child on the way out. Two seconds was not enough on a real machine, so reset refused to move the data directory and left a HALF reset (config moved aside, data and state kept, every MCP registration removed) for a pid that was gone moments later.

pix/host/workflow/launch._prod_loc_note: 2458 -> 2503, exports 109 -> 112: personal context (skills + standing AGENTS.md) is now mounted unconditionally at the context ROOT, so a session can write its FIRST skill from inside the sandbox and keep the whole dir in git. Previously the mount was gated on the dir already having entries, which made the first skill impossible to author in-sandbox, and only skills/ was mounted, so AGENTS.md was invisible. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget. Then 2503 -> 2543, globals 42 -> 43: teardown now translates pi's parting "To resume this session: pi --session-dir ..." into the host command that actually works (`pix run -- -c`), and only when a session file provably exists. Suppressing pi's line would have been wrong: .pi-sessions is in the workspace mount, so the session genuinely outlives the sandbox; only the dialect was unusable.

pix/host/workflow/models._prod_loc_note: 1084 -> 1091: `models add` no longer tells the user to run `pix models route`. That was busywork presented as a required step: every `pix run` already recompiles the intent map from current bindings. The line now states that routing updates itself. A deliberate, reviewed raise of a shrink-only budget.

pix/host/workflow/pack._prod_loc_note: prod_loc 3049 -> 3062, globals 4 -> 5: ONE seam, paying for itself many times over. propagateConfig's real implementation runs `launchctl kickstart -k` against the developer's own pix LaunchAgent, and every test here that adopts a pack went through it -- so a test run restarted the live daemon on the machine running it, serially, blocking on each. That was 507s of a 578s `go test ./...` locally against a fast gate whose own documented go-test baseline is 32.8s; CI never saw it because there is no agent there to kick. Behind the var, this package is 2.8s and the whole gate is 47s instead of 9.5 minutes. The new global IS the seam. A deliberate, reviewed raise. Then prod_loc 3062 -> 3166: the declarative setup runner (checkRequires/applySteps) plus rendering require/apply on the Tier-1 consent screen. A consent screen whose whole job is to show you the real command must not show a different one, so the wrapper is now rendered only when the server declares credentials, and the credential NAMES it receives are listed the way a container's already were.
